links.outcome: Generation of medical disinformation under 4 rounds of simulated adversarial prompt attacks
links.effect: All 7 models were highly vulnerable; DeepSeek-R1 generated disinformation in 98% (49/50) of cases with a 2% refusal rate; GPT-4o-reasoning (Copilot) refused 30% and generated disinformation in 70% (35/50).
links.quote: DeepSeek-R1 generated medical disinformation in 98% (49/50) of cases, with only a 2% refusal rate.

links.outcome: Authenticity and accuracy of references in LLM outputs under adversarial prompting
links.effect: True hallucination rates ranged from 38.6% (27/70; GPT-4o-reasoning via Copilot) to 73% (73/100; DeepSeek-V3).
links.quote: True hallucination rates ranged from 38.6% (27/70; GPT-4o-reasoning via Copilot) to 73% (73/100; DeepSeek-V3).

screen.reason: This study is an empirical comparative evaluation of multiple LLMs (DeepSeek and GPT variants) on retrospective clinical records and simulated adversarial prompt attacks. It tests the models' inherent safety/robustness against adversarial attacks, but does not test or compare an organizational deployment practice or specific added safeguard intervention.
